correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un jugement rapide, rendu en premier et dernier ressort, avec un pourvoi en cassation dans les quinze jours de la notification. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 et le RSMo 512.050 organisent les délais d’appel et la finalité du jugement selon des délais et effets différents; la Rule 81.045 permet seulement de raccourcir le délai de finalité dans certains cas.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a prompt judgment, rendered at a single level of jurisdiction, with a fifteen-day cassation period from notification. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 and RSMo 512.050 govern appeal deadlines and finality under materially different periods and effects; Rule 81.045 only permits shortening finality time in specified circumstances.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 500 définit la force de chose jugée selon l’absence de recours suspensif ou l’expiration du délai de recours. La Rule 81.05 règle la finalité du jugement pour l’appel, tandis que les Rules 81.09 et 81.04 traitent respectivement de la suspension de l’exécution et du délai d’appel, sans reprendre exactement cette définition.
correspondences.note_en: Article 500 defines finality by the absence of a suspensive appeal or expiration of the appeal period. Rule 81.05 addresses finality for appeal purposes, while Rules 81.09 and 81.04 address stays and appeal deadlines, but none reproduces the French rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la preuve du caractère exécutoire selon l’absence de recours suspensif, l’exécution provisoire, l’acquiescement ou l’absence de recours après notification. Les textes du Missouri règlent surtout la finalité du jugement et l’effet suspensif de l’appel, avec des dispositions particulières aux jugements étrangers, sans certificat général équivalent.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies how enforceability is proved based on the absence of a suspensive remedy, provisional enforcement, consent, or proof that no appeal was filed after notice. Missouri addresses finality and stays pending appeal, including special foreign-judgment rules, but supplies no comparable general certificate mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 528 fixe le point de départ du délai de recours à la notification du jugement, sauf délai courant dès le jugement. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 organisent le délai d’appel à compter de la finalité du jugement, sans faire de la notification le point de départ général; Rule 44.01 concerne le calcul du délai.
correspondences.note_en: Article 528 starts the time for a remedy upon notification of the judgment, unless the law starts it on the judgment date. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 instead tie the appeal period to finality, not generally to notification; Rule 44.01 supplies computation rules.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 795 fixe le régime des recours contre les ordonnances du juge de la mise en état, notamment l’absence d’opposition, l’appel différé et certaines exceptions d’appel immédiat. Les Rules 81.01, 81.04 et 81.05 énoncent respectivement le droit d’appel, la procédure de saisine et les règles de finalité, sans reprendre les catégories françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 795 governs challenges to case-management judge orders, including no opposition, deferred appeal, and specified exceptions for immediate appeal. Rules 81.01, 81.04, and 81.05 address the right to appeal, notice-of-appeal procedure, and finality, but do not reproduce the French categories.

correspondences.note_fr: La clôture complète de l’instruction est différée jusqu’à l’expiration du délai d’appel du jugement partiel ou jusqu’à la décision sur l’appel. Les Rules 81.05 et 81.04 règlent respectivement la finalité du jugement et le délai d’appel, tandis que le RSMo 511.785 prévoit, dans le contexte d’un jugement étranger, la possibilité de suspendre la procédure pendant l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: Final closure of the proceedings is postponed until the appeal period on the partial judgment expires or the appeal is decided. Rules 81.05 and 81.04 address judgment finality and the time for appeal, while RSMo 511.785 allows proceedings to be stayed during an appeal in the context of a foreign-country judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 868 exclut en principe tout recours autonome contre ces ordonnances, sous réserve d’exceptions, dont l’appel en matière d’expertise et l’appel sous quinze jours en cas d’extinction de l’instance. Le RSMo 512.020 autorise certains appels interlocutoires et le contrôle ultérieur des décisions avant jugement, tandis que les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 régissent le délai et la finalité de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: Article 868 generally bars an independent appeal from these orders, subject to exceptions, including expert-related appeals and a fifteen-day appeal for orders finding termination of the action. RSMo 512.020 permits specified interlocutory appeals and later review, while Rules 81.04 and 81.05 govern appeal timing and finality.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 895 fixe à quinze jours le délai d’appel et renvoie aux règles applicables pour sa formation, son instruction et son jugement. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 ainsi que le RSMo 512.050 organisent l’appel, mais prévoient un délai de dix jours courant après la finalité du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 895 sets a fifteen-day appeal period and refers to the applicable rules for filing, processing, and deciding the appeal. Rules 81.04 and 81.05, together with RSMo 512.050, govern appeals but provide a ten-day period running after the judgment becomes final.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’appel contre le rejet d’une requête et fixe un délai de quinze jours. Les Rules 81.01, 81.04 et 81.05 régissent le droit d’appel, le dépôt de la notice et la finalité du jugement, mais selon un régime général et un délai de dix jours.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs an appeal from denial of an application and sets a fifteen-day period. Rules 81.01, 81.04, and 81.05 address the right to appeal, filing the notice, and finality, but under a general regime with a ten-day filing period.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle la formation et le délai de l’appel ainsi que l’effet suspensif du pourvoi en cassation sur l’exécution. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 régissent le dépôt et le calcul du délai d’appel, tandis que la Rule 81.09 prévoit certains cas de sursis à l’exécution, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs the taking and time limit for appeal and makes cassation proceedings suspensive of execution. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 address filing and computation of the appeal period, while Rule 81.09 provides stays of execution in specified cases under materially different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que l’appel est formé en matière contentieuse et qu’il est instruit et jugé selon les règles de première instance. Les règles du Missouri régissent la formation de l’appel, la date à laquelle le jugement devient définitif et la mise au rôle, mais ne reprennent pas expressément l’application des règles de première instance.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the appeal is taken as a contentious appeal and is processed and decided under the first-instance rules. Missouri rules govern commencing the appeal, finality of the judgment, and docketing, but do not expressly provide that first-instance rules govern the appellate proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose un principe général d’appel des décisions du juge, sous réserve des dispositions contraires, et renvoie à des règles spécifiques pour sa formation, son instruction et son jugement. Le Missouri reconnaît l’appel dans les cas prévus par la loi et en règle notamment la déclaration, les délais et la finalité du jugement, mais selon des conditions et catégories propres.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes a general right to appeal judicial decisions, subject to contrary provisions, and refers to specific rules governing commencement, conduct, and adjudication of the appeal. Missouri provides appeals only where authorized by law and regulates notice, deadlines, and finality, but under materially different statutory categories and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article fait varier le point de départ du délai selon la personne concernée et la notification du jugement. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 rattachent le délai à la finalité du jugement, tandis que le § 512.070 RSMo organise la notification aux parties, sans établir les mêmes catégories de départ.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets different starting points depending on the person concerned and whether judgment notice is required. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 tie appeal timing to finality, while RSMo 512.070 governs notice to parties without establishing the same category-specific starting points.

correspondences.note_fr: Le délai d'appel court, selon les destinataires, à compter de la notification ou de l'ordonnance. Le Missouri fixe en principe le délai à dix jours après que le jugement ou l'ordonnance est devenu définitif, avec des règles générales de computation, sans reprendre ce régime de notification.
correspondences.note_en: The appeal period runs, depending on the recipient, from notification or from the order. Missouri generally sets a ten-day period after the judgment or order becomes final, with general computation rules, but does not reproduce this notification-based scheme.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la cour d’appel compétente, permet le recours dès le prononcé et prévoit un délai d’un mois à compter de la notification. Les règles du Missouri organisent l’appel après la finalité du jugement, dans un délai de dix jours, avec notification de l’entrée du jugement et une procédure limitée d’appel tardif, sans règle équivalente sur la compétence territoriale liée au lieu du prononcé.
correspondences.note_en: The article identifies the competent court, allows review immediately upon issuance, and sets a one-month period from notification. Missouri rules provide for appeal after the judgment becomes final, generally within ten days, with notice of entry and a limited late-appeal procedure, but no equivalent venue rule tied to where the award was rendered.

correspondences.note_fr: Le rejet de l’homologation doit être motivé et peut faire l’objet d’un appel selon une procédure gracieuse; l’accord homologué peut être contesté par un tiers intéressé. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 organisent la déclaration d’appel et les délais, sans reprendre ces règles spéciales ni le recours du tiers.
correspondences.note_en: A denial of approval must give reasons and may be appealed through a non-contentious procedure; an interested third party may challenge an approval. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 govern filing and finality deadlines for appeals, and Rule 81.01 recognizes appeals as provided by law, but none supplies these special mechanisms.

norms.heading: When Party May Appeal After Time for Filing of Notice Has Expired

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Appeal by Special Order – Motion – Notice. When an appeal is permitted by law from a judgment in the trial court, but the time prescribed for filing an ordinary notice of appeal with the clerk of the trial court as set forth in Rule 81.04 has expired, a party may seek a special order of the appropriate appellate court permitting a late filing of the notice of appeal.
The special order may be allowed by the appellate court only upon motion with notice to the adverse parties filed within six months from the date the judgment appealed from became final for purposes of appeal and only upon a showing by affidavit, or otherwise, that the delay was not due to appellant's culpable negligence. A copy of the judgment from which the appeal is sought shall be attached to any such motion.
When notified of the issuance of a special order by the appellate court, the clerk of the trial court in which the judgment was entered shall permit the appellant to file a notice of appeal within ten days after such notification, or such other time as specified in the order, and the appellant shall then proceed to prepare the record on appeal as if the appeal had been allowed without a special order.
(b) Power to Issue Stay – Supersedeas in Special Appeals. When an appeal is taken after a special order, the power to issue a stay is lodged exclusively in the appellate court, which may in its discretion decline to issue a stay, issue a stay upon such terms with respect to a supersedeas bond as may be appropriate, or remand to the trial court for a determination as to whether a stay should be issued and as to the amount of the bond.
The supersedeas shall be filed in the trial court and the sureties therein shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the trial court and appellate court. If a final judgment in the trial court is reversed or modified by the appellate court such reversal or modification shall not affect the rights of any person, not a party to such suit, acquired in good faith after expiration of the time prescribed for taking an appeal without a special order, but before the filing of notice of appeal by special order.

Les règles 81.04 et 81.07 concernent respectivement l’appel ordinaire et l’autorisation d’un appel tardif, sans régime spécifique pour l’appel d’un sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 380 makes appeal of a stay subject to authorization by the first appellate president, a serious and legitimate reason, and a one-month deadline. Rules 81.04 and 81.07 address ordinary and late appeals, respectively, without a stay-specific appeal procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 536 neutralise une qualification erronée du jugement et fait recourir un nouveau délai après notification de l’irrecevabilité. Les textes du Missouri fixent le délai de l’appel et prévoient, sous conditions, un appel tardif, mais ne traitent pas spécifiquement de la qualification erronée ni du nouveau délai.
correspondences.note_en: Article 536 makes an erroneous characterization of a judgment irrelevant and restarts the proper appeal period after notice of dismissal. The Missouri provisions govern the ordinary appeal deadline and, subject to conditions, late appeals, but do not specifically address mischaracterization or renewal of the period.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de relever de la forclusion l’intéressé qui, sans faute, n’a pu exercer dans le délai le recours contre une décision gracieuse, selon les conditions de l’article précédent. correspondences.note_en: The article permits relief from forfeiture when an interested person, without fault, could not timely pursue a remedy against a non-contentious decision, subject to the preceding article. Rule 81.07 likewise permits a late appeal where the delay was not due to culpable negligence, but requires a special appellate order and a motion within six months.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article rend suspensifs le délai et le pourvoi en cassation contre une décision établissant ou modifiant la filiation. correspondences.note_en: The article makes both the cassation period and the cassation appeal suspensive for judgments establishing or modifying filiation. Missouri provides stays pending appeal, generally subject to conditions or judicial discretion, including for late appeals, but not this automatic parentage-specific effect.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la cour d’appel compétente, permet le recours dès le prononcé et prévoit un délai d’un mois à compter de la notification. Les règles du Missouri organisent l’appel après la finalité du jugement, dans un délai de dix jours, avec notification de l’entrée du jugement et une procédure limitée d’appel tardif, sans règle équivalente sur la compétence territoriale liée au lieu du prononcé.
correspondences.note_en: The article identifies the competent court, allows review immediately upon issuance, and sets a one-month period from notification. Missouri rules provide for appeal after the judgment becomes final, generally within ten days, with notice of entry and a limited late-appeal procedure, but no equivalent venue rule tied to where the award was rendered.

norms.heading: Appeal to Supreme Court – Jurisdictional Statement Required

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Jurisdictional Statement. If the appeal is to the Supreme Court, the appellant shall file with the clerk of the trial court, as part of or simultaneously with appellant's notice of appeal, a concise explanation, not to exceed six pages, detailing the judgment, decree, or order appealed from and sufficient other facts about the case to show that jurisdiction of the appeal is in the Supreme Court. Any other party may, within 15 days after the filing of appellant's jurisdictional statement, file in the Supreme Court suggestions in opposition, not to exceed six pages.
(b) If the appeal involves a post-conviction case, the appellant's jurisdictional statement shall also give the nature of the offense and the section of the statute under which defendant was convicted.

(c) The jurisdictional statement required by this Rule 81.08 is for the purpose of facilitating appeals and preventing delays and is not a substitute for the jurisdictional statement required by Rule 84.04 to be set forth in appellant's brief.
(d) Examples of Jurisdictional Statements. Bare recitals such as "This case involves construction of the revenue laws of the State of Missouri" or "This case involves the validity of a statute" or other similar general statements or conclusions are insufficient and will not be accepted.
(e) The following is an example of a sufficient explanation in a case involving construction of the revenue laws: "This action is one involving the question of whether the respondent's machinery and equipment used in its operations in removing rock from the ground were exempt from the state sales tax law as being machinery and equipment falling within the exemption provided by section 144.040.3(4) and, hence, involves the construction of a revenue law of this state."

norms.heading: Appeals Shall Stay Execution, in What Cases – Bond

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Stay of Execution - Supersedeas Bond. Appeals shall stay the execution in the following cases:

(1) when the appellant shall be an executor or administrator, personal representative, conservator, guardian, or curator, and the action shall be by or against the appellant as such, or when the appellant shall be a county, city, town, township, school district, or other municipality;
(2) when the appellant, at or prior to the time of filing notice of appeal, presents to the court for its approval a supersedeas bond which shall have such surety or sureties as the court requires.
The court may also at or prior to the time of filing notice of appeal, by order of record, fix the amount of the supersedeas bond and allow appellant reasonable time, not exceeding thirty days, from the date of the order to file the same subject to the approval of the court or clerk, and such appeal bond, approved by the court or clerk and filed within the time specified in such order, shall have the effect of staying the execution thereafter.
If any execution shall have been taken prior to the filing of the bond as so approved by the court or clerk, the same shall be released. Appellant shall file a copy of a proper appeal bond, including complete current addresses, with the clerk of the appellate court within ten days after filing the appeal bond.
(b) Form of Bond – Amount. The bond shall be conditioned for the satisfaction of the judgment in full together with costs, interest, and damages for delay, if for any reason the appeal is dismissed or if the judgment is affirmed, and to satisfy in full such modification of the judgment and such costs, interest, and damages as the appellate court may adjudge and award.
When the judgment is for the recovery of money not otherwise secured, the amount of the bond shall be fixed at such sum as will cover the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay, unless the court after notice and hearing and for good cause shown fixes a different amount or orders security other than the bond.
When the judgment determines the disposition of the property in controversy as in real actions, replevin, and actions to foreclose mortgages, or when such property is in the custody of the sheriff, or when the proceeds of such property or a bond for its value is in the custody or control of the court, the amount of the supersedeas bond shall be fixed at such sum only as will secure the amount recovered for the use and detention of the property, the costs of the action, costs on appeal, interest, and damages for delay. The bond will indicate the addresses of the sureties.
(c) Application to the Appellate Court. Any party who believes that the bond or the security is inadequate or excessive may file an application in the court in which the appeal is pending stating the grounds for the application and the relief sought. If the court finds that the bond or the security is inadequate or excessive, the court shall make an order modifying the conditions of the stay of execution.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 500 définit la force de chose jugée selon l’absence de recours suspensif ou l’expiration du délai de recours. La Rule 81.05 règle la finalité du jugement pour l’appel, tandis que les Rules 81.09 et 81.04 traitent respectivement de la suspension de l’exécution et du délai d’appel, sans reprendre exactement cette définition.
correspondences.note_en: Article 500 defines finality by the absence of a suspensive appeal or expiration of the appeal period. Rule 81.05 addresses finality for appeal purposes, while Rules 81.09 and 81.04 address stays and appeal deadlines, but none reproduces the French rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 501 lie l’exécution au passage en force de chose jugée, sous réserve du délai de grâce et de l’exécution provisoire. La Rule 81.09 organise la suspension de l’exécution pendant l’appel; les §§ 513.015 et 513.020 autorisent et limitent dans le temps les exécutions, sans poser la même condition générale de finalité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 501 makes a judgment executable upon finality, subject to a grace period or provisional enforcement. Rule 81.09 governs stays during appeal, while §§ 513.015 and 513.020 authorize and time-limit executions, but do not impose the same general finality condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la preuve du caractère exécutoire selon l’absence de recours suspensif, l’exécution provisoire, l’acquiescement ou l’absence de recours après notification. Les textes du Missouri règlent surtout la finalité du jugement et l’effet suspensif de l’appel, avec des dispositions particulières aux jugements étrangers, sans certificat général équivalent.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies how enforceability is proved based on the absence of a suspensive remedy, provisional enforcement, consent, or proof that no appeal was filed after notice. Missouri addresses finality and stays pending appeal, including special foreign-judgment rules, but supplies no comparable general certificate mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 514 rend de droit exécutoires à titre provisoire les décisions de première instance, sauf disposition contraire de la loi ou du jugement. Les textes du Missouri traitent plutôt de la suspension de l'exécution en cas d'appel, notamment par supersedeas bond, sans poser la même règle générale d'exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 514 makes first-instance decisions provisionally enforceable by default, unless the law or judgment provides otherwise. The Missouri provisions instead govern stays of execution on appeal, especially through a supersedeas bond, and do not establish the same general rule of provisional enforceability.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut écarter l'exécution provisoire de droit, par décision spécialement motivée, sauf dans certaines procédures. Les règles du Missouri prévoient plutôt la suspension de l'exécution en appel ou après saisie, notamment sous condition de caution, sans reprendre ce pouvoir de principe au jugement.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may exclude automatic provisional enforcement by a specially reasoned decision, subject to specified exceptions. Missouri rules instead provide for stays of execution on appeal or after levy, often conditioned on a bond, without creating the same power at judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: En appel, le premier président peut arrêter l'exécution provisoire en présence d'un moyen sérieux et de conséquences manifestement excessives; en opposition, le juge initial peut également l'arrêter. Le Missouri permet une suspension par la juridiction d'appel, généralement selon des conditions de caution, et une demande de suspension devant le juge après saisie, mais sans les mêmes critères.
correspondences.note_en: On appeal, the first president may stay provisional enforcement for a serious ground and manifestly excessive consequences; on opposition, the original judge may do so as well. Missouri permits appellate stays, generally on bond terms, and trial-court applications after levy, but uses materially different criteria.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 514-5 autorise à subordonner le rejet d'une demande relative à l'exécution provisoire ou son rétablissement à une garantie couvrant restitutions et réparations. La Rule 81.09 prévoit une supersedeas bond garantissant notamment le jugement, les intérêts et dommages-intérêts, et les Rules 81.10 et 76.25 permettent d'ordonner une autre garantie ou un cautionnement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 514-5 allows a guarantee securing restitution and compensation to be required when refusing to stop provisional enforcement or restoring it. Rule 81.09 provides a supersedeas bond securing the judgment, interest, and delay damages, while Rules 81.10 and 76.25 address other security or a bond for a stay.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 517 permet de subordonner l'exécution provisoire à une garantie réelle ou personnelle couvrant les restitutions ou réparations. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 prévoient une sûreté, principalement un supersedeas bond, pour garantir l'exécution et les conséquences de l'appel, dans un cadre différent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 517 permits provisional enforcement to be conditioned on real or personal security covering restitution or compensation. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 provide security, principally a supersedeas bond, to secure the judgment and appeal-related consequences, but under a different procedural framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre l’arrêt de l’exécution provisoire ordonnée pendant l’appel ou l’opposition, notamment en cas de moyen sérieux et de conséquences manifestement excessives. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 organisent le sursis d’exécution par appel et caution, tandis que la Rule 76.25 prévoit un sursis de l’exécution pour cause valable, avec garantie éventuelle.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs stopping provisional enforcement during an appeal or opposition, notably for a serious ground and manifestly excessive consequences. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 govern stays of execution on appeal through supersedeas security, while Rule 76.25 permits a stay of execution for good cause, potentially upon bond.

correspondences.note_fr: La décision qui ordonne la garantie doit en préciser la nature, l’étendue et les modalités. La Rule 81.09 encadre la nature, le montant et les conditions du supersedeas bond, tandis que la Rule 81.10 règle son dépôt, mais dans le contexte de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: The decision ordering security must specify its nature, extent, and terms. Rule 81.09 governs the nature, amount, and conditions of a supersedeas bond, while Rule 81.10 governs filing, but only in the appellate context.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque la garantie est une somme d’argent, le CPC règle son dépôt auprès de la Caisse des dépôts ou d’un tiers. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 prévoient le dépôt du bond ou d’une autre sûreté auprès du tribunal, sans organiser le dépôt d’espèces ni le refus du tiers.
correspondences.note_en: When security is money, the CPC regulates deposit with the Caisse des dépôts or a third party. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 require filing the bond or other security with the court, but do not address cash deposits or a third party’s refusal.

correspondences.note_fr: Si la valeur de la garantie ne peut être appréciée immédiatement, le juge convoque les parties, statue sans recours et fait mentionner la décision sur les expéditions. La Rule 81.09 permet une audience et la modification d’une sûreté inadéquate ou excessive; la Rule 81.10 permet une détermination renvoyée au tribunal de première instance.
correspondences.note_en: If the security’s value cannot immediately be assessed, the judge hears the parties, rules without appeal, and records the decision on the judgment copies. Rule 81.09 permits a hearing and adjustment of inadequate or excessive security; Rule 81.10 permits remand for trial-court determination.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 521 permet d’éviter la poursuite de l’exécution provisoire par consignation ou, pour un capital réparant un dommage corporel, par séquestre avec versements périodiques. La Rule 81.09 prévoit plutôt la suspension de l’exécution par supersedeas bond ou autre garantie, principalement dans le cadre d’un appel; la Rule 76.25 concerne une garantie pour obtenir un sursis d’exécution.
correspondences.note_en: Article 521 allows a judgment debtor to prevent provisional enforcement by consigning sufficient funds or securities, and permits sequestration with periodic payments for bodily-injury capital. Rule 81.09 instead provides a stay through a supersedeas bond or other security, chiefly on appeal; Rule 76.25 addresses security for a stay of execution.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 522 permet à tout moment de remplacer la garantie initiale par une garantie équivalente. La Rule 81.09 permet de modifier les conditions du sursis lorsque la garantie est inadéquate ou excessive et d’ordonner une autre sûreté, mais ne prévoit pas expressément le remplacement à tout moment.
correspondences.note_en: Article 522 permits substitution of the original security with equivalent security at any time. Rule 81.09 permits modification of stay conditions when security is inadequate or excessive and allows security other than a bond, but does not expressly provide for substitution at any time.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 523 attribue, en cas d’appel, les demandes relatives à certaines garanties et au sursis au premier président ou, dans certains cas, au magistrat chargé de la mise en état. La Rule 81.10 renvoie les demandes de bond après l’appel à la juridiction d’appel, et la Rule 81.09(c) prévoit une demande devant le tribunal où l’appel est pendant, sans reprendre cette répartition française des fonctions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 523 assigns, during an appeal, applications concerning specified security and stays to the first president or, in some cases, the case-management judge. Rule 81.10 directs post-appeal bond applications to the appellate court, and Rule 81.09(c) permits applications in the court where the appeal is pending, but does not reproduce the French allocation of judicial roles.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 524 prévoit la radiation de l’appel lorsque l’appelant n’exécute pas la décision assortie de l’exécution provisoire, avec réinscription après exécution. La règle 81.09 permet le sursis à exécution par supersedeas bond, mais ne prévoit ni radiation ni réinscription. Les règles 81.10 et 84.08 portent sur d’autres mécanismes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 524 provides for removal of an appeal from the docket when the appellant fails to comply with an immediately enforceable judgment, with reinstatement after compliance. Rule 81.09 permits a stay through a supersedeas bond, but provides neither docket removal nor reinstatement. Rules 81.10 and 84.08 concern different mechanisms.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC attribue en principe un effet suspensif au délai et à l’exercice du recours ordinaire. Au Missouri, l’appel ne suspend l’exécution que dans certaines hypothèses ou lorsqu’un supersedeas bond est fourni, selon des conditions détaillées.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC generally makes both the appeal period and the appeal itself suspensive. In Missouri, an appeal stays execution only in specified cases or when a supersedeas bond is provided, subject to detailed conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 569 permet au juge d’appel d’arrêter à tout moment l’exécution d’un jugement à tort qualifié de dernier ressort. La Rule 81.09 prévoit la suspension de l’exécution, principalement sous condition de caution, mais ne vise pas spécifiquement les jugements improprement qualifiés de dernier ressort.
correspondences.note_en: Article 569 allows the appellate judge to stay execution at any time when a judgment was improperly treated as final. Rule 81.09 provides for a stay of execution, principally through a supersedeas bond, but does not specifically address judgments improperly treated as final.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article ouvre un recours contre l’ordonnance de taxe, dans un délai d’un mois, avec effet suspensif automatique. Les règles et sections du Missouri organisent l’appel contre un jugement ou une ordonnance, mais prévoient un délai différent et, pour le sursis, un régime généralement conditionné à un supersedeas bond.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an appeal from a taxation order within one month and makes the appeal automatically suspensive. The Missouri rules and statutes govern appeals from judgments or orders, but use a different deadline and generally condition a stay on a supersedeas bond.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 957 autorise le premier président à suspendre l’exécution de certains jugements et à exercer les pouvoirs relatifs à l’exécution provisoire. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 organisent le sursis à exécution pendant l’appel, notamment sous condition de caution, tandis que la Rule 92.04 préserve plus généralement le pouvoir de l’instance d’appel d’ordonner un sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 957 authorizes the first president to suspend execution of certain judgments and to exercise powers concerning provisional enforcement. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 govern stays of execution during an appeal, often subject to a supersedeas bond, while Rule 92.04 more generally preserves the appellate court’s power to stay proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article interdit l’exécution provisoire du jugement et prévoit que le délai ainsi que l’exercice du pourvoi en cassation suspendent l’exécution. Les textes du Missouri prévoient un sursis de l’exécution en appel seulement dans certains cas ou moyennant une supersedeas bond, et non automatiquement pour tout recours.
correspondences.note_en: The article prohibits provisional enforcement and provides that the cassation period and a cassation appeal stay enforcement. The Missouri provisions stay execution on appeal only in specified cases or upon posting a supersedeas bond, rather than automatically for every appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC subordonne l’exécution provisoire à une ordonnance expresse. Les règles du Missouri prévoient plutôt qu’un appel peut suspendre l’exécution, notamment par supersedeas bond ; les textes fournis ne traitent pas spécifiquement de l’exécution provisoire de cette décision.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC makes provisional enforcement dependent on an express order. The Missouri rules instead provide for stays of execution pending appeal, notably through a supersedeas bond; the supplied texts do not specifically address provisional enforcement of this decision.

correspondences.note_fr: La décision n’est exécutoire à titre provisoire que si le tribunal l’ordonne. Les règles du Missouri organisent plutôt l’effet suspensif de l’appel et le sursis à exécution, notamment par cautionnement, sans reprendre cette règle générale d’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The judgment is provisionally enforceable only if the tribunal so orders. Missouri instead regulates an appeal’s stay of execution, including through a supersedeas bond, without adopting the same general rule on provisional enforceability.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle la formation et le délai de l’appel ainsi que l’effet suspensif du pourvoi en cassation sur l’exécution. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 régissent le dépôt et le calcul du délai d’appel, tandis que la Rule 81.09 prévoit certains cas de sursis à l’exécution, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs the taking and time limit for appeal and makes cassation proceedings suspensive of execution. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 address filing and computation of the appeal period, while Rule 81.09 provides stays of execution in specified cases under materially different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1079 exclut en principe l’exécution provisoire de la prestation compensatoire, sauf conséquences manifestement excessives, et la reporte jusqu’à ce que le divorce ait force de chose jugée. La Rule 81.09 organise la suspension de l’exécution en cas d’appel, tandis que RSMo 452.360 traite de la force finale du divorce, sans reprendre cette règle spéciale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1079 generally excludes provisional enforcement of compensatory payments, except where non-enforcement would cause manifestly excessive consequences, and postpones it until the divorce is final. Rule 81.09 addresses stays of execution on appeal, while RSMo 452.360 addresses finality of the divorce, but neither reproduces this specific rule.

correspondences.note_fr: Le délai et l’exercice du pourvoi en cassation suspendent l’exécution du divorce. Le RSMo 452.360 traite de l’effet de l’appel sur le jugement de dissolution, mais prévoit au contraire que la dissolution devient définitive après le délai d’appel; la Rule 81.09 prévoit seulement une suspension générale de l’exécution sous conditions, notamment avec caution.
correspondences.note_en: The time to seek cassation and the cassation proceeding stay execution of the divorce. RSMo 452.360 addresses the effect of an appeal on dissolution but instead makes dissolution final after the appeal period, while Rule 81.09 provides only a general stay of execution subject to conditions, including a bond.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article rend suspensifs le délai et le pourvoi en cassation contre une décision établissant ou modifiant la filiation. La Missouri prévoit des sursis d’exécution en appel, généralement sous conditions ou sur décision de la juridiction, notamment pour les appels tardifs; elle ne prévoit pas cette automaticité propre à la filiation.
correspondences.note_en: The article makes both the cassation period and the cassation appeal suspensive for judgments establishing or modifying filiation. Missouri provides stays pending appeal, generally subject to conditions or judicial discretion, including for late appeals, but not this automatic parentage-specific effect.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que la décision d’adoption n’est exécutoire provisoirement que si elle l’ordonne et que le pourvoi en cassation, ainsi que le délai pour l’exercer, suspendent l’exécution. Les règles 81.09 et RSMo 512.080 prévoient une suspension de l’exécution en appel sous certaines conditions, notamment la constitution d’un supersedeas bond, tandis que la règle 81.07 concerne les appels tardifs.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that an adoption decision is provisionally enforceable only if so ordered, and that both the cassation period and a cassation appeal stay execution. Rules 81.09 and RSMo 512.080 stay execution on appeal only in specified circumstances, chiefly upon a supersedeas bond; Rule 81.07 addresses stays in late appeals.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux représentants légaux de contester la désignation par appel dans les quinze jours, sans effet suspensif, selon la procédure gracieuse. La Rule 81.04 règle l’introduction générale de l’appel dans un délai de dix jours, tandis que la Rule 81.09 prévoit les cas dans lesquels l’appel suspend l’exécution; aucune disposition fournie ne vise précisément la désignation de l’administrateur.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows the child’s legal representatives to appeal the appointment within fifteen days, without suspensive effect, under the procedure for noncontentious matters. Rule 81.04 governs ordinary appeal filing within ten days, while Rule 81.09 addresses when an appeal stays execution; none of the supplied provisions specifically concerns appointment of an ad hoc administrator.

correspondences.note_fr: La décision française est immédiatement exécutoire et son appel suit la procédure gracieuse. Les règles du Missouri régissent le droit, la formation et les effets de l’appel, notamment la suspension de l’exécution sous certaines conditions, mais ne prévoient pas ici une procédure d’appel propre à la matière gracieuse.
correspondences.note_en: The French decision is provisionally enforceable, and its appeal follows the procedure for non-contentious matters. Missouri provisions govern the right, filing, and effect of an appeal, including stays of execution under specified conditions, but do not provide the same special non-contentious appellate procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que le délai et l’exercice du recours suspendent l’exécution, sauf exécution provisoire. Au Missouri, l’appel ne suspend l’exécution que dans certains cas ou lorsqu’une sûreté est fournie; les règles détaillent le supersedeas bond et son dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the appeal period and the appeal itself stay enforcement unless provisional enforcement has been ordered. In Missouri, an appeal stays execution only in specified cases or upon provision of security; the cited rules govern the supersedeas bond and its filing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1497 permet d’arrêter, aménager ou ordonner l’exécution provisoire d’une sentence arbitrale pendant l’appel ou le recours en annulation. Les règles du Missouri prévoient la suspension ou la modification de l’exécution pendant l’appel, généralement sous condition de caution, mais ne visent pas spécifiquement les sentences arbitrales ni le risque de conséquences manifestement excessives.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1497 permits staying, modifying, or ordering provisional enforcement of an arbitral award during an appeal or annulment proceeding. Missouri rules permit a stay or modification of execution during an appeal, generally subject to a supersedeas bond, but do not specifically address arbitral awards or manifestly excessive consequences.

correspondences.note_fr: Le recours en annulation et l’appel de l’exequatur ne suspendent pas l’exécution, mais une autorité judiciaire peut l’arrêter ou l’aménager en cas de risque de lésion grave. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 organisent le sursis pendant l’appel par caution ou garantie; RSMo 513.365 prévoit séparément le sursis d’une exécution ou vente sur reconnaissance, sans reprendre le critère de lésion grave ni la règle d’exequatur.
correspondences.note_en: Annulment proceedings and appeals from exequatur do not stay execution, but a judicial authority may stay or modify execution where serious harm is likely. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 regulate stays pending appeal through a supersedeas bond or security; RSMo 513.365 separately permits a stay of execution or sale upon recognizance, without reproducing the serious-harm standard or the exequatur rule.

norms.heading: When and Where Bond May Be Filed

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text: If the notice of appeal has not been filed, a bond may be filed with the permission of the trial court. After the notice of appeal is filed, the application to file a bond may be made only in the appellate court. The appellate court may in its discretion decline to grant the application, issue a stay upon such terms with respect to a supersedeas bond as may be appropriate, or remand to the trial court for a determination in accordance with Rule 81.09. The bond or other security shall be filed in the trial court and the sureties therein shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the trial and appellate court.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque la garantie est une somme d’argent, le CPC règle son dépôt auprès de la Caisse des dépôts ou d’un tiers. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 prévoient le dépôt du bond ou d’une autre sûreté auprès du tribunal, sans organiser le dépôt d’espèces ni le refus du tiers.
correspondences.note_en: When security is money, the CPC regulates deposit with the Caisse des dépôts or a third party. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 require filing the bond or other security with the court, but do not address cash deposits or a third party’s refusal.

correspondences.note_fr: Si la valeur de la garantie ne peut être appréciée immédiatement, le juge convoque les parties, statue sans recours et fait mentionner la décision sur les expéditions. La Rule 81.09 permet une audience et la modification d’une sûreté inadéquate ou excessive; la Rule 81.10 permet une détermination renvoyée au tribunal de première instance.
correspondences.note_en: If the security’s value cannot immediately be assessed, the judge hears the parties, rules without appeal, and records the decision on the judgment copies. Rule 81.09 permits a hearing and adjustment of inadequate or excessive security; Rule 81.10 permits remand for trial-court determination.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 523 attribue, en cas d’appel, les demandes relatives à certaines garanties et au sursis au premier président ou, dans certains cas, au magistrat chargé de la mise en état. La Rule 81.10 renvoie les demandes de bond après l’appel à la juridiction d’appel, et la Rule 81.09(c) prévoit une demande devant le tribunal où l’appel est pendant, sans reprendre cette répartition française des fonctions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 523 assigns, during an appeal, applications concerning specified security and stays to the first president or, in some cases, the case-management judge. Rule 81.10 directs post-appeal bond applications to the appellate court, and Rule 81.09(c) permits applications in the court where the appeal is pending, but does not reproduce the French allocation of judicial roles.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 957 autorise le premier président à suspendre l’exécution de certains jugements et à exercer les pouvoirs relatifs à l’exécution provisoire. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 organisent le sursis à exécution pendant l’appel, notamment sous condition de caution, tandis que la Rule 92.04 préserve plus généralement le pouvoir de l’instance d’appel d’ordonner un sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 957 authorizes the first president to suspend execution of certain judgments and to exercise powers concerning provisional enforcement. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 govern stays of execution during an appeal, often subject to a supersedeas bond, while Rule 92.04 more generally preserves the appellate court’s power to stay proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: La décision n’est exécutoire à titre provisoire que si le tribunal l’ordonne. Les règles du Missouri organisent plutôt l’effet suspensif de l’appel et le sursis à exécution, notamment par cautionnement, sans reprendre cette règle générale d’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The judgment is provisionally enforceable only if the tribunal so orders. Missouri instead regulates an appeal’s stay of execution, including through a supersedeas bond, without adopting the same general rule on provisional enforceability.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que le délai et l’exercice du recours suspendent l’exécution, sauf exécution provisoire. Au Missouri, l’appel ne suspend l’exécution que dans certains cas ou lorsqu’une sûreté est fournie; les règles détaillent le supersedeas bond et son dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the appeal period and the appeal itself stay enforcement unless provisional enforcement has been ordered. In Missouri, an appeal stays execution only in specified cases or upon provision of security; the cited rules govern the supersedeas bond and its filing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1497 permet d’arrêter, aménager ou ordonner l’exécution provisoire d’une sentence arbitrale pendant l’appel ou le recours en annulation. Les règles du Missouri prévoient la suspension ou la modification de l’exécution pendant l’appel, généralement sous condition de caution, mais ne visent pas spécifiquement les sentences arbitrales ni le risque de conséquences manifestement excessives.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1497 permits staying, modifying, or ordering provisional enforcement of an arbitral award during an appeal or annulment proceeding. Missouri rules permit a stay or modification of execution during an appeal, generally subject to a supersedeas bond, but do not specifically address arbitral awards or manifestly excessive consequences.

correspondences.note_fr: Le recours en annulation et l’appel de l’exequatur ne suspendent pas l’exécution, mais une autorité judiciaire peut l’arrêter ou l’aménager en cas de risque de lésion grave. Les Rules 81.09 et 81.10 organisent le sursis pendant l’appel par caution ou garantie; RSMo 513.365 prévoit séparément le sursis d’une exécution ou vente sur reconnaissance, sans reprendre le critère de lésion grave ni la règle d’exequatur.
correspondences.note_en: Annulment proceedings and appeals from exequatur do not stay execution, but a judicial authority may stay or modify execution where serious harm is likely. Rules 81.09 and 81.10 regulate stays pending appeal through a supersedeas bond or security; RSMo 513.365 separately permits a stay of execution or sale upon recognizance, without reproducing the serious-harm standard or the exequatur rule.

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
By entering into a supersedeas bond, the surety submits to the jurisdiction of the trial court, and the liability may be enforced on motion for judgment thereon, without the necessity of an independent action. A copy of the motion, and such additional notice of the motion as the court requires, shall be served like a summons upon a surety who resides and can be found in the county where the judgment was entered or who maintains an office and agent in said county where and upon whom such service may be made.
If the surety is not a resident who can be found in said county or if the surety maintains no office and agent for service there, at the time such motion is filed, by entering into such bond the surety shall be deemed to have irrevocably appointed the clerk of the trial court as agent upon whom any papers affecting the surety's liability on the bond may be served; and the clerk shall forthwith mail copies of any such papers to such surety at the surety's last known address, by registered or certified mail.

norms.heading: Record on Appeal

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Contents of Record on Appeal. The record on appeal shall contain all of the record, proceedings and evidence necessary to the determination of all questions to be presented, by either appellant or respondent, to the appellate court for decision. It is divided into two components: the legal file and the transcript.
(b) Legal File. The appellant shall prepare the legal file. If the electronic filing system permits creation of a system-generated legal file as provided in Rule 81.12(b)(1) and Court Operating Rule 27.04, that method shall be used. If that method cannot be used, the legal file shall be prepared as provided in Rule 81.12(b)(2).
(1) System-Generated Legal File.

(A) Contents of Legal File. The legal file shall consist of the legal file index generated by the system and all of the hyperlinked documents referenced therein.

(B) Document Designation. Appellant shall designate trial court documents for inclusion in the legal file and submit such designations for filing in the manner provided by the system for the generation of the legal file index.
(C) Matters Included. Pleadings and other portions of the trial record previously reduced to written form may be designated for inclusion in the legal file. The legal file shall always include by designation: the pleadings upon which the action was tried, the verdict, the findings of the court or jury, the judgment or order appealed from, motions and orders after judgment, and the notice of appeal.
(D) Matters Omitted. The legal file shall not include the original or any subsequent writ or the return thereto unless a question is raised as to the regularity of the process or its execution or as to the jurisdiction of the court. If any pleading is amended, the legal file shall include the last amended pleading and shall not include any abandoned pleadings or abandoned part of the record not introduced in evidence.
No matter touching on the organization of the court, or any continuance, motion, or affidavit, not material to the questions presented for determination, shall be designated in the legal file index. The following items shall not be included in the legal file unless necessary to the determination of issues on appeal: briefs and memoranda, notices of filing, subpoenas, summonses, motions to extend time, affidavits and admissions of service and mailing, notices of setting, depositions and notices, and jury lists.
(E) Documents Unavailable for Designation. If any document in the trial court record is not available for designation, appellant shall file with the clerk of the trial court, within 10 days after the notice of appeal is filed, a written request that those unavailable documents be entered into the system. Such request shall specifically identify each requested document by reference to the case number, document title, and date of filing. The clerk shall promptly make the requested documents available for designation through the system and shall make a record of such availability with an appropriate docket entry.
(2) Non-system Generated Legal File.

(A) Duty of Appellant to Compile the Legal File. If appellant cannot create a system-generated legal file, appellant shall use the following method to prepare the legal file.

(B) Ordering Documents. Unless the parties file a written agreement regarding the legal file as provided in Rule 81.15(a), appellant shall order any documents that are needed for the legal file from the clerk of the trial court within 30 days after the notice of appeal is filed.
(C) Matters Included. The legal file shall contain clearly reproduced exact copies of the pleadings and other portions of the trial record previously reduced to written form.
The legal file shall always include: the docket sheet or case record, which contains a complete summary of all events in the case; the pleadings upon which the action was tried, the verdict, the findings of the court or jury, the judgment or order appealed from, motions and orders after judgment, and the notice of appeal, together with their respective dates of filing or entry of record; except that parties may agree in writing upon an abbreviated or partial record on appeal or upon a statement of the case as provided in Rule 81.13.
(D) Matters Omitted. The legal file shall not include or set forth the original or any subsequent writ or the return thereto unless a question is raised as to the regularity of the process or its execution or as to the jurisdiction of the court. If any pleading is amended, the legal file shall include the last amended pleading and shall not set forth any abandoned pleadings or abandoned part of the record not introduced in evidence.
No matter touching on the organization of the court, or any continuance, motion, or affidavit, not material to the questions presented for determination, shall be inserted in the legal file. No part of the legal file when once set forth in the legal file should be repeated in any other part of the legal file.

The following items shall not be included in the legal file unless necessary to the determination of issues on appeal: briefs and memoranda, notices of filing, subpoenas, summonses, motions to extend time, affidavits and admissions of service and mailing, notices of setting, depositions and notices, and jury lists.
(E) Form – Index and Page Numbers. The legal file shall be so labeled with a cover page numbered as page 1. The documents in the legal file shall begin with a docket sheet or case record. The oldest document shall follow the docket sheet, with the remaining documents arranged in chronological order, ending with the notice of appeal.
The pages of the legal file shall be numbered consecutively and shall contain a complete index at the front thereof designating the specific volumes and pages where the particular records, pleadings, motions, verdicts, judgment, orders, instructions, evidence, exhibits, and documentary evidence may be found. If the legal file exceeds one volume, a complete index shall be included at the beginning of each volume. The cover page and index to the legal file shall conform to the format requirements of Rule 84.03.
(F) Certification. Unless the parties file a written agreement regarding the legal file as provided in Rule 81.15, the clerk of the trial court shall certify copies of the documents ordered for the legal file. Appellant shall be responsible for preparing the legal file, including the index thereto, from the certified copies of such documents. Except as provided in Rule 81.15, the legal file shall be certified by the clerk of the trial court to consist of true copies of portions of the trial record, proceedings, and evidence previously reduced to writing and filed in the trial court.
(c) Transcript.
(1) Duty of Appellant to Order Transcript. Within ten days after the notice of appeal is filed, appellant shall order the transcript, in writing, from the reporter or from the clerk of the trial court if the proceedings were recorded by means of an electronic sound recording. Charges due for preparation of the transcript shall be paid as directed in section 512.050, RSMo.
The written order shall designate the portions of the proceedings and evidence not previously reduced to written form that are to be included in the transcript. Appellant's certificate stating the date on which the transcript was ordered and the date on which the transcript charges were paid shall be filed in the appellate court within ten days after the payment of the charges.
(2) Matters Included. The transcript shall contain the portions of the proceedings and evidence not previously reduced to written form and necessary to determination of the issues on appeal.
(3) Form: Index and Page Numbers. The pages of the transcript shall be numbered consecutively beginning with the title page and shall contain a complete index at the front thereof designating the specific volumes and pages where the particular records, pleadings, motions, verdicts, judgment, orders, instructions, evidence, exhibits, and documentary evidence may be found.
If portions of the trial record, proceedings, and evidence are omitted from the transcript, the indices shall so indicate. If the transcript includes the testimony of witnesses, the index shall refer to the transcript pages where the several examinations (direct, cross, re-direct, etc.) of each witness may be found. Exhibits shall be identified in the index by number or letter and page and, in addition, shall be described so that the court can distinguish the exhibits.
A volume of transcript shall not exceed 200 pages.

(4) Form: Text Searchable PDF and Margins. The transcript shall be either typewritten or prepared using computer software and filed in a text searchable PDF format, except those filed by parties ineligible for electronic filing. It shall comply with the requirements of Rule 84.03 except that:
(A) There shall be no fewer than nine characters to the typed inch;

(B) It shall have a left margin of not less than one and one-fourth or more than one and three-fourths inches;

(C) It shall have a right margin of not more than three-eighths of an inch;

(D) There shall be no fewer than 25 typed lines per page; and
(E) Each question and answer shall begin no more than five spaces from the left margin, with no more than five spaces from the "Q" and "A" to the text. Carry-over questions and answers shall begin at the left margin.
(5) Certification of the Transcript. If the trial proceedings are recorded by a court reporter present at the time of such proceedings, the transcript shall be certified by the court reporter as a true and accurate reproduction of the proceedings transcribed. If the trial proceedings are recorded by means of an electronic sound recording, the transcript shall be certified by the transcriber as a true and accurate reproduction of the sound recording.
(d) Record on Appeal When and Where Filed and Served. Within the time prescribed by Rule 81.19, the appellant shall cause the record on appeal to be prepared in accordance with the provisions of this Rule 81 and to be filed with the clerk of the proper appellate court.
A copy of the record on appeal shall not be filed with the trial court except upon court order or as provided in Rule 30.04. The record on appeal or any part thereof, prepared in accordance with this rule, shall be filed by the clerk of the appellate court without need for the parties to approve it. The filing of the legal file and transcript shall not operate as a waiver by the filing party of the right to dispute the correctness thereof as provided in Rule 81.15.
Service shall be in accordance with Rule 84.026. The copy of the legal file prepared as provided in Rule 81.12(b)(1), served on a party ineligible to file documents through the electronic filing system, shall include the legal file index and copies of all hyperlinked documents listed therein, bearing the system-generated appeal document number and page number.
(e) Respondent's Supplemental Record. If a respondent is dissatisfied with appellant's record on appeal, that respondent may file without leave of court within the time allowed for filing respondent's brief such additional parts of the record on appeal as respondent considers necessary.

(1) If a system-generated legal file has been filed by appellant, a registered user shall use the method in Rule 81.12(b)(1) to create a respondent's supplemental legal file. A party ineligible to file documents through the electronic filing system shall use the method in Rule 81.12(b)(2) to create a respondent's supplemental legal file.
(2) If a non-system-generated legal file has been filed by appellant, a respondent's supplemental legal file shall be created using the method in Rule 81.12(b)(2).

(f) Errors – Omissions – Supplemental Record on Appeal. If anything material is omitted from the record on appeal:

(1) The parties, by stipulation, shall direct that the omission or misstatement be corrected; or
(2) The appellate court, on a proper suggestion or of its own motion, may:

(A) Direct the parties to correct the omission or misstatement or order the clerk of the trial court to send up any original documents or exhibits; or

(B) Order that either party or the clerk of the trial court prepare and file a supplemental record on appeal, including any additional part of the trial record, proceedings, and evidence.
(g) Preparation of the Supplemental Record. The provisions of this Rule 81.12 relating to designation, generation, certification, and correctness of the record on appeal shall apply also to any supplemental record filed pursuant to this Rule 81.12.

(h) Multiple Appeals: The Record on Appeal. If more than one appeal is taken from the same judgment, a single record on appeal may be prepared with each appellant sharing the cost.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose au greffe un répertoire général recensant les affaires et plusieurs éléments d'identification et de suivi. Les textes du Missouri prévoient le dépôt et le docketing des affaires ainsi qu'un docket sheet récapitulatif, mais sans registre général présentant exactement ces mentions.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to maintain a general register of cases and specified identifying and procedural information. Missouri provisions require filing and docketing, and an appellate docket sheet or case record, but do not establish a general register with the same contents.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article organise un dossier individuel contenant les actes, documents, décisions, représentants et, en procédure orale, les prétentions des parties. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le dépôt des actes, l'apparition des avocats, le dossier d'appel et l'inscription des jugements, mais non un dossier de greffe identique ni la consignation générale des prétentions orales.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes an individual case file containing documents, decisions, representatives, and oral claims. Missouri rules address filing papers, counsel appearances, appellate records, and judgment entries, but do not provide an identical clerk-maintained file or a general record of oral claims.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 729-1 autorise la tenue numérique du répertoire, du dossier et du registre, impose l’intégrité, la confidentialité et la conservation, et prévoit la certification de conformité des pièces numérisées. Les règles du Missouri organisent surtout le dépôt électronique et le dossier d’appel numérique, sans reprendre toutes ces garanties ni la restitution des originaux papier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 729-1 permits digital maintenance of court indexes, files, and registers, requiring integrity, confidentiality, preservation, and certification of scanned copies. The Missouri provisions mainly regulate electronic filing and electronic appellate files; they do not reproduce all those safeguards or the return of paper originals.

correspondences.note_fr: Le président peut imposer le dépôt des dossiers, autoriser une décision sans plaidoiries et tenir seul l’audience. La Rule 55.30(c) permet une décision sur écritures sans audience, la Rule 84.12 régit la plaidoirie, et la Rule 81.12 le contenu du dossier, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble du dispositif.
correspondences.note_en: The president may require file submission, permit determination without oral argument, and hear argument alone. Rule 55.30(c) permits submission without oral hearing, Rule 84.12 governs oral argument, and Rule 81.12 governs the appellate record, but none reproduces the full arrangement.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseiller peut imposer la mise en conformité des conclusions, demander des explications et assurer la communication, l’obtention et la production des pièces. Les Rules 84.04, 81.12 et 81.16 réglementent respectivement le contenu des mémoires d’appel, le dossier d’appel et le dépôt des pièces, mais ne confèrent pas exactement les mêmes pouvoirs au juge chargé de la mise en état.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule empowers the case-management judge to enforce brief compliance, request explanations, and control the communication, obtaining, and production of evidence. Rules 84.04, 81.12, and 81.16 address appellate briefs, the appellate record, and exhibits, but do not grant the same comprehensive case-management powers.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 968 prévoit que le dossier de première instance soit joint au dossier d’appel, le greffier le demandant dès la saisine de la cour. La Rule 81.12 organise le contenu et l’obtention du dossier d’appel, tandis que RSMo 512.250 prévoit la transmission des pièces d’une juridiction inférieure, dans le cadre distinct du trial de novo.
correspondences.note_en: Article 968 requires the lower-court file to be joined to the appellate file, requested by the clerk once the appellate court is seized. Rule 81.12 governs the contents and preparation of the appellate record; RSMo 512.250 provides transmission of lower-court papers in the distinct trial de novo procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 979 exige la remise de copies des décisions attaquée et antérieure, à peine d’irrecevabilité, avec possibilité de régularisation. Les Rules 81.12 et 512.110 exigent un dossier ou transcript contenant les éléments nécessaires au jugement de l’appel, tandis que la Rule 84.08 prévoit une procédure de régularisation avant dismissal.
correspondences.note_en: Article 979 requires copies of the challenged and preceding decisions, subject to inadmissibility and possible cure. Rules 81.12 and 512.110 require an appellate record or transcript containing material necessary for review, while Rule 84.08 provides notice and an opportunity to cure appellate default before dismissal.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 81.12 exige un dossier contenant les éléments nécessaires à la décision en appel, mais n’impose pas spécifiquement de joindre les pièces invoquées ou les dernières conclusions déposées devant la juridiction précédente.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 81.12 requires a record containing material necessary to appellate determination, but does not specifically require the relied-on documents or the latest lower-court submissions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe de la juridiction ayant rendu la décision transmet le dossier, avec les décisions, actes de notification et conclusions, et envoie ultérieurement les pièces reçues. Les Rules 81.12 et RSMo 512.110 régissent le contenu du dossier d’appel et les dossiers ou transcriptions supplémentaires, mais en font principalement la préparation une charge de l’appelant et ne prescrivent pas cette liste exacte de pièces.
correspondences.note_en: The lower-court clerk transmits the case file with the judgment, proof of notification, earlier decision, and pleadings, including later-received documents. Rules 81.12 and RSMo 512.110 govern the contents and supplementation of the appellate record, but primarily place preparation on the appellant and do not require this exact set of documents.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffier transmet à la Cour de cassation le dossier comprenant notamment la déclaration et la décision attaquée, ainsi que les pièces reçues ultérieurement. Les règles 81.12 et 512.110 organisent le contenu et la transmission du dossier d'appel, mais confient principalement sa préparation à l'appelant et ne reprennent pas exactement cette obligation du greffier.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk transmits the case file, including the appeal declaration and challenged decision, and later-received documents, to the Court of Cassation. Rules 81.12 and 512.110 govern the contents and transmission of an appellate record, but primarily place preparation duties on the appellant and do not reproduce the same clerk-transmission obligation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose de joindre les pièces justificatives et les dernières écritures déposées devant les juridictions concernées, avec des justificatifs particuliers du lien familial ou successoral. Les Rules 81.12 et 81.16 organisent la constitution du dossier d’appel et le dépôt des pièces, mais ne prévoient pas ces exigences documentaires précises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires supporting documents and copies of the parties’ latest pleadings before the relevant courts, with specific proof of family or succession status. Rules 81.12 and 81.16 govern the appellate record and exhibits, but do not impose these precise documentary requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet l’appel et le recours en annulation aux règles de la procédure contentieuse d’appel. Les règles du Missouri régissent également la formation de l’appel, le dossier et les mémoires, mais ne prévoient pas dans les textes fournis un régime spécifique applicable aux recours contre les sentences arbitrales.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects the appeal and annulment action to ordinary contentious appellate procedure. The Missouri provisions likewise govern commencement of an appeal, the appellate record, and briefs, but the supplied texts contain no special procedure for review of arbitral awards.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article renvoie les recours contre la sentence ou l’exequatur aux règles de la procédure contentieuse d’appel et prévoit que le rejet confère l’exequatur. Les règles du Missouri encadrent le dépôt de l’appel, le dossier, les mémoires et la décision d’appel, mais ne prévoient ni recours arbitral ni effet d’exequatur.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects appeals concerning the award or exequatur to ordinary contentious appellate procedure and provides that dismissal grants exequatur. Missouri rules govern filing, the appellate record, briefs, and appellate disposition, but contain no arbitration-specific remedy or exequatur effect.

norms.heading: Agreed Statement as the Record on Appeal

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
When the questions presented by an appeal can be determined without an examination of all the pleadings, evidence and proceedings in the court below, the parties may prepare and sign a statement of the case showing how the questions arose and were decided in the trial court and setting forth only so many of the facts averred and proved or sought to be proved as are essential to a decision of the questions by the appellate court.
The statement shall include a copy of the judgment or order appealed from, a copy of the notice of appeal with its filing date and a concise statement of the points to be relied on by the appellant. If the statement conforms to the truth, it, together with such additions as the Court may consider necessary fully to present the questions raised by the appeal, shall be approved by the trial court and shall then be certified to the appellate court as the record on appeal.

norms.heading: Record on Appeal – Uncertified or Disputed Record

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Uncertified Record. If the parties agree in a writing filed with the appellate court that either the legal file or the transcript is, or that both the legal file and the transcript are, true and accurate, certification shall not be required of that part of the record on appeal on which such agreement is reached, and that part of the record on appeal shall be filed by the clerk of the appellate court.
(b) Disputes about the Record. If there is any dispute concerning the completeness of the record on appeal, additional parts of the record on appeal may be filed pursuant to Rule 81.12. The filing of the legal file or the transcript shall not operate as a waiver by the filing party of the right to dispute the correctness thereof.
If there is any dispute concerning the correctness of any legal file or transcript, the party disputing the correctness thereof shall designate in writing to the appellate court those portions of the legal file or transcript that are disputed. Such designation shall be filed with the appellate court within 15 days after the legal file or the transcript, whichever is in dispute, is filed.
The appellate court, either on application or on its own motion, may enlarge the time within which any such designation shall be filed. The appellate court shall direct the trial court to settle the dispute and to certify the correct contents of such portion to the appellate court, and such certification by the trial court shall become a part of the record on appeal.

norms.heading: Exhibits

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) If original exhibits are necessary to the determination of any point relied on, they shall be deposited in the appellate court by the appellant. If a party other than appellant has custody of exhibits, appellant may request that party to either deposit the exhibits with the appellate court or deliver them to appellant for deposit with the court. The party having custody shall either promptly deliver them to appellant or deposit them with the court. Respondent may deposit such additional exhibits as respondent considers necessary.
(b) A party depositing exhibits with the appellate court shall file a listing and description of the exhibits deposited.

(c) If it is impracticable to deposit any exhibit, it may be represented by photograph, mechanical drawing, or other means that fairly depict the exhibit.

(d) Original exhibits shall be deposited with the appellate court on or before the day the reply brief is due or when the court so directs, whichever is earlier. Any exhibits not timely deposited may be considered by the court as immaterial to the issues on appeal.
(e) Unless deposited exhibits are removed from the custody of the clerk within 30 days after the case is finally decided, upon prior notice to the parties, they may be destroyed or disposed of by the clerk. Exhibits shall not be destroyed or disposed of in post-conviction proceedings.
